applied_evidence.statement: The existing 7.2 m candidate width remains inside the photo-derived front-width interval; no user measurement is introduced.

Owner-confirmed topology fixes descent as west beyond the main rear plane, then a left turn and south to the low courtyard. The two Scene runs remain low-confidence metric inference: existing provisional width, rise split, total rise and horizontal run-length magnitudes are reused rather than adding a new measurement.
Only the ordering is user-confirmed. The nominal timber z and support height remain low-confidence revisable Scene inference.

Photos 3 and 4 show exposed portions of the same raised timber terrace and support that the previous candidate footprint was likely too short. The retained 3.0 m depth is a low-confidence revisable Scene inference, not a measurement; exact floor continuity through the occluded masonry/stair zone remains unresolved.

After the owner-confirmed stair route was materialized, the previous rectangular timber-deck proxy visibly intersected the westbound stair. Because the exact hidden timber contour is not photo-resolved and is secondary for the LEGO goal, the represented deck envelope is conservatively clipped at the already-existing y=7.8 masonry landing rear boundary. This is a reversible Scene simplification, not a claim that the real deck terminates there and not a new measurement.
